After years of broaching the subject, we finally have Isgarren's approval. Even with Mabon advocating for me, Vass's final words won the day—surprised I am not—but now the real work begins. As Akeem and Mabon review my initial designs and make suggestions for the eventual forging process, I sit here, pondering the earlier arguments. I can still hear our leader's leery remarks at my proposal.  

Even after all these years, it's hard not to feel like the source of his greatest shame. I am his accidental "wizard," his brazen misstep. I can remember flashes—the trepidation in his face, the way his fingers clutched that ancient shadowstone staff as he worked through the designs of his revised ritual. I recall the balmy thicket he'd brought me to, wherever it was, and the irritating buzz of large insects. After the ritual, my mind had hardly calmed amidst its haze before I was spirited to his tower in the sky.  

I never want to sound ungrateful for what he sacrificed, but for every day he bitterly speaks of "lessons learned" it somewhat sours the compassion he offered back then. I don't know how long I'll be able to stomach it, certainly not for as long as the Divcia Nava extends my life—I still age at the pokiest snail's pace, after all. Unlike the others, I don't come from an exceptionally long-lived people. Still, maybe there's a comfort in that.  

***  

The forging is complete, and I'm exhausted. "The Heart of the Obscure," we're calling it. Akeem was surprised and touched by my suggestion, to which I stated that its obscurity lies in its potential. He and Mabon are spending time with it, putting it through its paces in the Mists. I'll have tests of my own once I've recovered.  

Ren came by to offer me his idea of praise. Said if I "kept at it for another few thousand years, I could be the next Gardesano," whoever that was. I took the compliment, though. Could've sworn I saw him crack a smile at the device. Felt good, like I truly belonged here in Amnytas, with the rest of them.

I held myself aloft for only half a day today—half as long as the day before. I can still hear Baraq's mirthful laughter as I was forced to use the stairs. Archivist Orestes banished him back to his studies with stories of when Baraq, Seraf, and Manikaz were also gildless—an attempt to cheer me up, I guess.  
  
Many days, I feel as though I will never be worthy and that I may never be the ideal mursaat. Orestes believes I am foolish for such thoughts, and he understands how I feel despite the vast ocean of years between us. I am not to be gilded with armor for a decade or so, but the archivist tells me I should relish my youth while I can—find "small joys" before the weight of expectation and history becomes too much to bear. How can one float with such burdens?  
  
Before we can become gilded, we must become magically adept; more attuned to this world's magical ebbs and flows. Many of my peers can become unseen and even hover for several days without a break. I phase well for a gildless my age, and while I struggle to fly like the others, one of my forebears has started to teach me transportation spells. A blink here, a portal there. I think I have a skill for it!  
  
Anyway, stopping here for today. One of the high researchers pulled Orestes away a moment ago. She looked concerned—a scrying eye was resting at her side. What has she seen? I wonder.

First Mate Eldan's Log, 1100 AE  
  
Went ashore today for a change of scenery—boss's orders. He thought we might find some plunder around here, something worth trading elsewhere in Tyria. Our luck must still be running south, though, 'cause there's nothing here. Nothing but the rustle of leaves and the chatter of animals for company, aye. Anything else is probably too far inland for us to reach.    
  
Ned's knee started aching again while we were searching, which usually means there's storms coming. The boss decided to wait until dark to cast away, so after he called off the search we sat around on the beach drinking spirits. The sunset was a thing o' beauty—all orange and red with li'l flecks of pink clouds floating by. With the breeze lifting our hair and the birds a-warbling, spirits wet on me lips, it was the closest thing to paradise I've felt in many a year.  
  
May Janthir always be a place o' rest.

strings.en:
I've been with the Astral Ward for a while and I still can't believe what I'm seeing. I knew that the wizards created fractals to observe the circumstances of our actions, but to see them HERE. In Tyria. Realized. It should be a scientist's dream, but...  

I'm with Lyhr and Frode at Droknar's Forge today. Lyhr is in shock. He didn't realize this was a fractal. His home. Dwarves who aren't made of stone... Why would Isgarren want to study this, and not tell him? How long as this fractal been active? I have so many questions... There aren't many left in the "real world." I don't know if this is a marvel or a miracle, but Lyhr isn't thrilled.  

I wonder how it must be to live in a false reality, yet still believe you actually exist. But...they DO actually exist. At least they do now. There are all sorts of moral implications that I can barely fathom...

Well, well. You've certainly earned my attention, %str1%.

What do they call you...the commander, was it? What a prestigious title. I've decided to make a special side project out of you, my dear. We're going to be seeing much more of each other, so you might as well cozy up and listen.

I warned you not to get in my way, but here we are. Next time I won't be quite so...gentle.

I simply can't wait to take you apart and see what makes you tick.

Tick-tock-tick.

—Scarlet (I don't need to hide behind silly codenames like "B" anymore, do I? This is quite exciting...)
